title: The best UConn women’s basketball player ever? Plus: A wild first day for NFL free agents
content:
The Pulse Newsletter 📣 | This is The Athletic’s daily sports newsletter. Sign up here to receive The Pulse directly in your inbox.

Good morning! Agree to something in principle today. Inside:

Yesterday, we mentioned Team USA’s previous struggle against Mexico in the World Baseball Classic. A fact I didn’t include: The Americans have not beaten Mexico in the WBC since 2006.

As of last night, the drought is over. Quickly:

Read more on the game here. Plenty more WBC action tonight, too. More on that in a bit:

I always think it’s very funny that this period of the NFL offseason is officially called “legal tampering.” I understand the league year starts tomorrow and that players were allowed to negotiate with teams yesterday, but … why can’t the league year just start yesterday? Or why can’t authorities let me speed from 8-9 a.m. and call it legal bad driving?

Anyway. We had a flurry of NFL deals agreed to in principle yesterday. Let’s hit some highlights extremely quickly:

For more context on that last concept, I asked Scoop City writer Jacob Robinson which move he was most surprised by and why — and he chose a different option:

💬 Evans landing in San Francisco. It’s weird to picture the 12-year veteran in any uniform other than the Buccaneers’. What does Evans have left? Hard to say after an injury-marred 2025, but a dominant Week 15 against Atlanta (six catches for 132 yards) suggests there’s still something in the tank for his age-33 season.

Three resources for you:

Phillies pay Luzardo
Is a baseball transaction allowed to happen when football is doing contract stuff and baseball is doing WBC stuff? The Phillies paid no mind as they agreed to a five-year, $135 million contract extension with Jesús Luzardo, who could’ve been a free agent after this season. Luzardo was awesome over 32 starts with a 3.92 ERA last year, though the 28-year-old’s advanced stats indicate he was a bit better than that number. Read our full report.

📰 Find more news here 24/7.

It is a cliche to say UConn women’s basketball is the definition of greatness. But this is the best program in the modern history of the sport. It has produced 12 national titles since 1995. Legends of this game have come from the school. Diana Taurasi, Maya Moore, Paige Bueckers. All massive, massive stars.

Sarah Strong might be better than all of them.

Jarring, right? I read the headline and nearly recoiled. But Chantel Jennings wrote a feature this morning that makes an extremely convincing case. One big point from me:

Strong, 20, also just seems completely impervious to any pitfalls of today’s game. Not a huge focus on NIL or social media in any regard. Nonetheless, all the experts, including her coach Geno Auriemma, seem dumbfounded by her.

Read the full story here.

📺 NBA: Celtics at Spurs
8 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock
I’m imagining a sign that screams “POSSIBLE FINALS MATCHUP” draped across the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. Be seated.

📺 WBC: Italy vs. Team USA
9 p.m. ET on FS1

The Italians are 2-0 in pool play, which means this game takes extra meaning considering Mexico’s loss last night. There is legit talent on this Italy roster, too: Jac Caglianone, Aaron Nola and young Dante Nori, the Phillies prospect who’s hit multiple homers in the WBC already. Another fun game.

📺 NCAAM: Gonzaga vs. Santa Clara
9 p.m. ET on ESPN
This is the WCC tournament final, and I just expect madness from here on out. If you want to load up, the Horizon League final is on before this at 7 p.m. ET.

📺 NHL: Oilers at Avalanche
10 p.m. ET on TNT and HBO Max
The best team in the NHL plays host to last year’s runners-up, who have been … fine. It’s at a point where everything — from great to awful — feels possible for Edmonton.

Are prediction markets just sports betting with different branding? Our experts tried to parse an answer. Super topical and worth a read this morning.

I loved this story on Brewers manager Pat Murphy and his time coaching the Netherlands in the 1980s. He holds the lessons of that experience dear.

Our weekly college baseball Top 25 is out. Please don’t perceive my Tigers right now.

Relevant for future use: An early look at the potential USWNT roster for the 2027 World Cup, particularly after the SheBelieves Cup win.

Most-clicked in the newsletter yesterday: Our story on Travis Kelce returning for a 14th season — and maybe not with the Chiefs. He later made this moot, agreeing to a new deal in K.C.

Most-read on the website yesterday: NFL free agency live blog, of course.

Correction: In yesterday’s newsletter, we referred to Boston University’s win over Navy as the Patriot League conference championship game. It was the semifinal. We apologize to the many fans who wrote in about the error, and BU will play fellow buzzer-beater-haver Lehigh in tomorrow’s title game. Still a Patriot League guy.

📫 That’s all for now! Say hello at thepulse@theathletic.com, and check out our other newsletters.
